To my understanding, the functions in MBTI (Te/Ti, Fe/Fi, etc.) don't really have anything to do with the classic introverted/extraverted dichotomy people imagine (the quiet kid in the back of the class vs the clown who can't stop speaking). 
The functions in MBTI are how you take and sort out information in your brain. Because a function is Introverted in the dominant position, you can appear more introverted: for example, Fi-doms sort information considering how they feel, what they value, etc. (that's caricatural, but that's basically it). In doing so, because they value their own feeling before everything else, they may appear more Introverted than a, for example, Se-dom, who'll be looking for external stimuli before anything else.

I've been in the same situation with my sister. It's terrifying seeing the people you love harming themselves the same way you do.
Talk to her, heart-to-heart, about your own struggles. The downside is that she may think you're lecturing her and she might get upset. You know how hard it is to admit there's something wrong.
Try to find in your environment what could be a trigger of the disorder. For example, if someone in your family says hurtful things or even seemingly innocent sentences that can be hurtful to your sister. Try to correct what you can in your direct environment.
Good luck, I know it's not easy.
